## *** NO qf_models ***
### - JUN protein group

```{r}
jun_accession <- "P05412"

jun_candidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    rd <- as.data.frame(
      SummarizedExperiment::rowData(
        qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]
      )
    )

    # Match JUN accession as a complete identifier,
    # including within semicolon-separated protein groups
    hit <- grepl(
      paste0("(^|[;|])", jun_accession, "($|[;|])"),
      as.character(rd$Protein.Group)
    )

    # Also search Protein.Ids where available
    if ("Protein.Ids" %in% names(rd)) {
      hit <- hit | grepl(
        paste0("(^|[;|])", jun_accession, "($|[;|])"),
        as.character(rd$Protein.Ids)
      )
    }

    hit[is.na(hit)] <- FALSE

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein.Group = as.character(rd$Protein.Group[hit])
    )
  })
)

print(jun_candidates, row.names = FALSE)
```
### - p_jun

```{r}
# Keep candidate groups present in the protein assays
jun_groups <- jun_candidates

# Require one unambiguous JUN protein group per pipeline
stopifnot(
  nrow(jun_groups) == 4,
  all(table(jun_groups$Software) == 1)
)

jun_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    se <- qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]

    protein_id <- jun_groups$Protein.Group[
      jun_groups$Software == software
    ]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Run = colnames(se),
      Log2_Intensity = as.numeric(
        SummarizedExperiment::assay(se)[protein_id, ]
      )
    )
  })
) |>
  left_join(sample_design, by = "Run") |>
  mutate(
    Genotype = case_when(
      grepl("^CTRL_", Condition) ~ "CTRL",
      grepl("^KO_", Condition) ~ "KO",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("CTRL", "KO")),
    Software = factor(Software, levels = names(qf_models))
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Genotype),
    grepl("Untreated|Baseline", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE)
  )

# Check sample coverage before plotting
jun_data |>
  group_by(Software, Batch, Genotype) |>
  summarise(
    Total = n(),
    Quantified = sum(is.finite(Log2_Intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)

p_jun <- ggplot(
  jun_data,
  aes(
    x = Genotype,
    y = Log2_Intensity,
    color = Genotype
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(Software ~ Batch, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(CTRL = "#0072B2", KO = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "JUN abundance across DIA pipelines",
    subtitle = "Untreated samples stratified by genotype and acquisition batch",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Normalized log2 JUN protein intensity"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p_jun)
```

# - protein estimability
```{r qc_protein_specific_estimability, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-specific design rank and contrast estimability
# ============================================================

qf_list <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Reconstruct contrast vectors from the existing design matrix
contrast_matrix <- t(vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts)),
  function(i) {
    reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Numerator[i], ] -
      reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Denominator[i], ]
  },
  numeric(ncol(design_matrix))
))

rownames(contrast_matrix) <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Verify that contrast coefficients match the design matrix
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(contrast_matrix),
    colnames(design_matrix)
  ),
  nrow(design_matrix) == nrow(design_data)
)

# Assign actual run names to the design matrix
rownames(design_matrix) <- as.character(design_data$Run)

# Confirm alignment
stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(design_matrix),
    as.character(design_data$Run)
  )
)

# Function to evaluate a single observed-sample pattern
check_pattern <- function(observed, X, C) {

  X_obs <- X[observed, , drop = FALSE]

  if (nrow(X_obs) == 0L) {
    return(c(
      Rank = 0,
      Full_Rank = 0,
      setNames(
        rep(0, nrow(C)),
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
      )
    ))
  }

  # QR rank of the observed design
  rank_obs <- qr(X_obs)$rank

  # SVD-based row-space test for contrast estimability
  sv <- svd(X_obs, nu = 0, nv = ncol(X_obs))

  tolerance <- max(dim(X_obs)) *
    max(sv$d) *
    .Machine$double.eps

  rank_svd <- sum(sv$d > tolerance)

  if (rank_svd == ncol(X_obs)) {

    estimable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(C))

  } else {

    null_basis <- sv$v[
      ,
      seq.int(rank_svd + 1L, ncol(X_obs)),
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    null_projection <- C %*% null_basis

    estimable <- apply(
      abs(null_projection),
      1,
      max
    ) < 1e-8
  }

  c(
    Rank = rank_obs,
    Full_Rank = as.integer(rank_obs == ncol(X)),
    setNames(
      as.integer(estimable),
      paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
    )
  )
}

protein_rank_results <- list()
protein_contrast_results <- list()

for (software in names(qf_models_68)) {

  cat("Checking:", software, "\n")

  se <- qf_models_68[[software]][["proteins"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # Align design matrix to the assay columns
  sample_idx <- match(colnames(x), design_data$Run)

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(sample_idx),
    !anyDuplicated(sample_idx)
  )

  X <- design_matrix[sample_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Finite protein measurements
  detected <- is.finite(x)

  # Group proteins with identical observed-sample patterns
  pattern_key <- apply(
    detected,
    1,
    function(z) paste0(as.integer(z), collapse = "")
  )

  unique_keys <- unique(pattern_key)

  pattern_results <- lapply(unique_keys, function(key) {

    observed <- which(
      strsplit(key, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "1"
    )

    check_pattern(
      observed = observed,
      X = X,
      C = contrast_matrix
    )
  })

  pattern_results <- do.call(
    rbind,
    pattern_results
  )

  # Map pattern results back to individual proteins
  protein_results <- pattern_results[
    match(pattern_key, unique_keys),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  protein_rank_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    Unique_Missingness_Patterns = length(unique_keys),
    Full_Rank_Proteins = sum(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Full_Rank_Percent = 100 * mean(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Median_Protein_Rank = median(
      protein_results[, "Rank"]
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  protein_contrast_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Contrast = planned_contrasts$Contrast,
    Estimable_Proteins = colSums(
      protein_results[
        ,
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(contrast_matrix))),
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    ),
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

protein_rank_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_rank_results
)

protein_contrast_estimability <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_contrast_results
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Estimable_Percent =
      100 * Estimable_Proteins / Total_Proteins
  )

cat("\nProtein-specific design rank:\n")
print(protein_rank_summary, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nProtein-specific contrast estimability:\n")
print(
  protein_contrast_estimability,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
The median protein-specific design rank is 12 for every software pipeline, matching the number of model coefficients. This means that nearly all proteins have sufficient observations across the experimental conditions and acquisition batches to estimate every coefficient in the proposed model. Importantly, the remaining rank-deficient proteins are not necessarily unusable. Some can still support particular biological contrasts.
Protein-specific design matrix diagnostics demonstrated high model identifiability across all four DIA analysis pipelines. Full-rank design matrices were obtained for 98.04% of AlphaDIA proteins, 97.70% of DIA-NN proteins, 99.99% of Spectronaut proteins, and 99.93% of MaxDIA proteins. Across the eleven planned biological contrasts, mathematical estimability exceeded 98.9% for every pipeline. These findings indicate that protein-level missingness is unlikely to substantially restrict differential abundance analysis. Nevertheless, direct comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour cisplatin treatments remain dependent on additive batch-effect assumptions because the treatment groups were acquired in separate batches. Therefore, subsequent statistical modeling will incorporate acquisition batch as a fixed effect, with cross-time-point comparisons interpreted cautiously.

# - upset all contrasts 83
```{r da_upset_all_contrasts, fig.width=13, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', eval=FALSE}

library(ComplexUpset)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# DA UpSet plots for all 11 experimental contrasts
# ============================================================

# Preserve software and contrast order
software_order <- names(inference_list)
contrast_order <- as.character(planned_contrasts$Contrast)

# Function to extract significant protein-group sets
get_da_sets <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- lapply(inference_list, function(results) {

    valid <- !is.na(results$contrast) &
      as.character(results$contrast) == contrast_name &
      is.finite(results$adjPval) &
      results$adjPval < 0.05 &
      !is.na(results$feature)

    unique(as.character(results$feature[valid]))
  })

  sets[software_order]
}

# Function to create one DA UpSet plot
make_da_upset <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- get_da_sets(contrast_name)
  # Sets with at least one significant protein
  active_software <- software_order[lengths(sets[software_order]) > 0]

  all_ids <- unique(unlist(sets, use.names = FALSE))

  if (length(all_ids) == 0L) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  presence <- data.frame(
    Protein = all_ids,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  for (software in software_order) {
    presence[[software]] <- all_ids %in% sets[[software]]
  }

  ComplexUpset::upset(
    presence,
    intersect = active_software,
    name = "DIA pipeline",
    sort_intersections_by = "cardinality",
    min_size = 1,
    width_ratio = 0.30,

    set_sizes = ComplexUpset::upset_set_size(
      geom = ggplot2::geom_bar(
        fill = unname(software_colors[active_software]),
        width = 0.65
      )
    ),

    base_annotations = list(
      "Significant protein-group intersections" =
        ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
          text = list(size = 3.2, vjust = -0.3)
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
          labels = scales::comma,
          expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
        )
    ),

    stripes = ComplexUpset::upset_stripes(
      colors = c("white", "#F5F7FA")
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Differential abundance overlap across DIA pipelines",
      subtitle = contrast_name,
      caption = paste(
        "BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05;",
        "exact protein-group identifier matching."
      )
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 16
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 12, color = "#667085"
      ),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 11
      ),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 9, color = "#344054"
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
        fill = "white", color = NA
      )
    )
}

# Generate and display each plot in the R Markdown output
for (contrast_name in contrast_order) {

  p <- make_da_upset(contrast_name)

  if (!is.null(p)) {
    print(p)
  }
}
```


# - Pairwise log2 fold-change comparison

```{r da_logfc_agreement_6h, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# Cross-pipeline log2 fold-change agreement
# Contrast: KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h
# ============================================================

target_contrast <- "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h"

software_order <- c(
  "AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA"
)

# 1. Extract log2 fold changes without filtering on significance
logfc_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {

    results <- inference_list[[software]]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(results$feature),
      logFC = as.numeric(results$logFC),
      Contrast = as.character(results$contrast)
    )
  })
) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Contrast == target_contrast,
    !is.na(Protein),
    is.finite(logFC)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Protein, Software, logFC)

# Ensure exact protein identifiers are unique within each pipeline
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(logfc_long[c("Protein", "Software")])
)

# 2. Create a protein-by-pipeline fold-change table
logfc_wide <- logfc_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Software,
    values_from = logFC
  )

# 3. Calculate pairwise correlations on shared proteins
pipeline_pairs <- combn(software_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)

logfc_pairwise_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(pipeline_pairs, function(pair) {

    paired <- logfc_wide[
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[1]]]) &
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[2]]]),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    x <- paired[[pair[1]]]
    y <- paired[[pair[2]]]

    data.frame(
      Pipeline_1 = pair[1],
      Pipeline_2 = pair[2],
      Shared_Proteins = length(x),
      Pearson_r = if (length(x) >= 3) {
        cor(x, y, method = "pearson")
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      Spearman_rho = if (length(x) >= 3) {
        cor(x, y, method = "spearman")
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      Same_Direction_Percent = if (length(x) > 0) {
        100 * mean(sign(x) == sign(y))
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    )
  })
)

print(
  logfc_pairwise_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        c(Pearson_r, Spearman_rho, Same_Direction_Percent),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# 4. Prepare six pairwise scatterplots
plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(pipeline_pairs, function(pair) {

    paired <- logfc_wide[
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[1]]]) &
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[2]]]),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    data.frame(
      Pair = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
      x = paired[[pair[1]]],
      y = paired[[pair[2]]]
    )
  })
)

# Shared axis limits across all six panels
axis_limit <- max(
  abs(c(plot_data$x, plot_data$y)),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# 5. Visualize agreement
p_logfc_agreement_6h <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = x, y = y)
) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#0072B2",
    alpha = 0.16,
    size = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Pair,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(-axis_limit, axis_limit),
    ylim = c(-axis_limit, axis_limit)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-pipeline agreement in protein log2 fold changes",
    subtitle = target_contrast,
    x = "Pipeline 1 log2 fold change",
    y = "Pipeline 2 log2 fold change",
    caption = paste(
      "All shared protein groups with finite log2 fold changes;",
      "exact protein-group identifier matching.",
      "Dashed line: y = x."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_logfc_agreement_6h)
```
Pairwise comparison of protein-level log2 fold changes for the KO versus CTRL contrast following 6 hours of cisplatin treatment revealed positive quantitative agreement across all four DIA analysis pipelines, although the strength of agreement varied. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN exhibited the strongest concordance (Pearson r = 0.845; Spearman ρ = 0.815), with 83.0% of shared protein groups showing consistent fold-change directions. Comparisons involving Spectronaut demonstrated intermediate agreement (Pearson r = 0.755–0.787), whereas MaxDIA exhibited weaker correlations with the other pipelines (Pearson r = 0.613–0.653) and lower directional concordance (72.4–72.9%). These findings indicate that differences in differential abundance detection are accompanied by variation in estimated protein abundance changes, particularly for MaxDIA. Although MaxDIA showed the highest precursor sequence–charge coverage per protein group, this did not translate into greater differential abundance detection or stronger quantitative agreement. Further assessment of fold-change magnitude and statistical uncertainty is needed to clarify the factors contributing to these differences.

# - abs_logfc


These results are important because they challenge our earlier hypothesis that MaxDIA detects fewer differentially abundant proteins primarily because it estimates smaller fold changes.

Comparison of absolute protein-level log2 fold-change distributions for the KO versus CTRL cisplatin 6h contrast showed that MaxDIA's lower number of significant protein groups was not accompanied by uniformly smaller estimated abundance changes. Among 7,474 protein groups with finite fold-change estimates in all four pipelines, the median absolute log2 fold change was 0.156 for AlphaDIA, 0.184 for DIA-NN, 0.215 for Spectronaut, and 0.181 for MaxDIA. Spectronaut exhibited the largest overall effect-size distribution, whereas MaxDIA showed magnitudes broadly comparable to DIA-NN and greater than AlphaDIA. These results do not support systematic attenuation of fold-change magnitudes as the principal explanation for MaxDIA's reduced differential abundance detection. Together with its weaker cross-pipeline fold-change correlations and higher median model residual variability, the findings suggest that differences in quantitative precision and statistical uncertainty may contribute to the observed discrepancies. Direct comparison of contrast-specific standard errors is required to evaluate this explanation.
# - statistical_precision
```{r da_statistical_precision_6h, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

target_contrast <- "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h"

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

# 1. Extract existing contrast-specific statistical results
precision_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {

    results <- inference_list[[software]]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(results$feature),
      Contrast = as.character(results$contrast),
      logFC = as.numeric(results$logFC),
      SE = as.numeric(results$se),
      t_stat = as.numeric(results$t)
    )
  })
) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Contrast == target_contrast,
    !is.na(Protein),
    is.finite(logFC),
    is.finite(SE),
    SE > 0,
    is.finite(t_stat)
  )

# Check unique protein identifiers within each pipeline
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(precision_long[c("Protein", "Software")])
)

# 2. Restrict to proteins with valid statistics in ALL four pipelines
common_precision_proteins <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {
    precision_long$Protein[precision_long$Software == software]
  })
)

precision_shared <- precision_long |>
  dplyr::filter(Protein %in% common_precision_proteins) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Absolute_t = abs(t_stat)
  )

cat(
  "Protein groups with valid statistics in all four pipelines:",
  length(common_precision_proteins), "\n"
)

# 3. Summary statistics
precision_summary <- precision_shared |>
  dplyr::group_by(Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_SE = median(SE),
    Q1_SE = unname(quantile(SE, 0.25)),
    Q3_SE = unname(quantile(SE, 0.75)),
    Median_Abs_t = median(Absolute_t),
    Q1_Abs_t = unname(quantile(Absolute_t, 0.25)),
    Q3_Abs_t = unname(quantile(Absolute_t, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(
  precision_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        -c(Software, N),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    ),
  n = Inf
)

# 4. Prepare data for visualization
precision_plot_data <- precision_shared |>
  dplyr::select(Software, SE, Absolute_t) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(SE, Absolute_t),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric = factor(
      Metric,
      levels = c("SE", "Absolute_t"),
      labels = c(
        "Contrast-specific standard error",
        "Absolute t-statistic"
      )
    )
  )

# 5. Plot distributions
p_precision <- ggplot(
  precision_plot_data,
  aes(x = Software, y = Value, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_violin(
    alpha = 0.55,
    trim = TRUE,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.16,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "white",
    color = "#344054",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Metric,
    scales = "free_y",
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = software_colors,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistical precision across pipelines",
    subtitle = paste0(
      target_contrast,
      " | Shared protein groups"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    # caption = paste(
    #   "Only proteins with finite log2FC, positive finite SE,",
    #   "and finite t-statistics in all four pipelines.",
    #   "Exact protein-group identifier matching."
    # )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_precision)
```
Despite comparable median absolute log2 fold changes between MaxDIA and DIA-NN (0.181 versus 0.184) among 7,474 commonly quantified protein groups, MaxDIA exhibited substantially higher contrast-specific standard errors (median 0.182 versus 0.085) and lower absolute t-statistics (median 0.951 versus 2.19). These findings suggest that reduced statistical precision, rather than systematically smaller estimated abundance changes, is a major contributor to MaxDIA's lower differential abundance detection rate. The results also demonstrate that greater precursor coverage per protein group does not necessarily translate into greater sensitivity for detecting differential protein abundance.

# - residual-variability
```{r residual-variability-comparison, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, dpi=300, out.width="100%"}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Existing fitted QFeatures objects
qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Extract residual sigma from existing msqrob2 StatModel objects
sigma_data <- lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

  assay <- qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]
  models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(assay)$msqrobModels

  data.frame(
    Protein = rownames(assay),
    Software = software,
    Sigma = vapply(
      models,
      function(m) {
        if (is.null(m)) return(NA_real_)

        sigma <- methods::slot(m, "params")$sigma

        if (length(sigma) != 1 ||
            !is.finite(sigma) ||
            sigma <= 0) {
          return(NA_real_)
        }

        as.numeric(sigma)
      },
      numeric(1)
    )
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Restrict to the 7,474 proteins used in the previous SE/t-statistic analysis
# and retain only proteins with valid sigma in all four pipelines
sigma_shared <- sigma_data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Protein %in% common_precision_proteins,
    is.finite(Sigma),
    Sigma > 0
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Protein) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Software) == 4) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = names(qf_models))
  )

# Summary statistics for matched proteins
sigma_summary <- sigma_shared |>
  dplyr::group_by(Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_Sigma = median(Sigma),
    Mean_Sigma = mean(Sigma),
    Q1_Sigma = unname(quantile(Sigma, 0.25)),
    Q3_Sigma = unname(quantile(Sigma, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat(
  "Matched proteins with valid residual sigma in all four pipelines:",
  dplyr::n_distinct(sigma_shared$Protein),
  "\n\n"
)

print(sigma_summary, n = Inf)

# Visualize residual variability
p_sigma <- ggplot(
  sigma_shared,
  aes(x = Software, y = Sigma, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    alpha = 0.65,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.15,
    fill = "white",
    color = "#344054",
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = software_colors) +
  scale_y_log10(
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Protein-level residual variability across DIA pipelines",
    subtitle = paste0(
      dplyr::n_distinct(sigma_shared$Protein),
      " matched protein groups with valid residual sigma"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Residual standard deviation, sigma (log10 scale)",
    caption = paste(
      "Existing batch-adjusted msqrob2 models.",
      "Identical protein groups compared across all four pipelines."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_sigma)
```
MaxDIA has substantially greater protein-level residual variability than the other three pipelines, even when we compare exactly the same 7,474 protein groups. On 7,474 matched protein groups, MaxDIA exhibited the highest residual variability (median σ = 0.309), approximately 2.22-fold greater than DIA-NN (0.139). This difference was accompanied by a 2.14-fold higher median standard error for the KO versus CTRL cisplatin 6h contrast, despite comparable median absolute log2 fold changes. These findings suggest that increased residual variability, rather than uniformly smaller estimated biological effects, contributes substantially to MaxDIA's lower number of statistically significant differentially abundant proteins. MaxDIA's lower differential abundance sensitivity is associated with substantially greater residual variability and higher statistical uncertainty, despite its greater precursor coverage per protein.

# - precision-all-contrasts
```{r precision-all-contrasts, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, dpi=300, out.width="100%", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Collect valid contrast-specific statistics
precision_all <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC),
      is.finite(se),
      se > 0,
      is.finite(t)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Abs_logFC = abs(logFC),
      SE = se,
      Abs_t = abs(t)
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Match proteins separately within each contrast
# Retain only proteins with valid results from all four pipelines
precision_matched <- precision_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Protein) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Software) == 4) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Contrast = factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order)
  )

# Summarize matched-protein statistics
precision_all_summary <- precision_matched |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_Abs_logFC = median(Abs_logFC),
    Median_SE = median(SE),
    Median_Abs_t = median(Abs_t),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(precision_all_summary, n = Inf)

# Prepare three metrics for a faceted comparison
precision_plot_data <- precision_all_summary |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Median_Abs_logFC, Median_SE, Median_Abs_t),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Median"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric = factor(
      Metric,
      levels = c("Median_Abs_logFC", "Median_SE", "Median_Abs_t"),
      labels = c(
        "Median absolute log2 fold change",
        "Median standard error",
        "Median absolute t-statistic"
      )
    )
  )

p_precision_all <- ggplot(
  precision_plot_data,
  aes(x = Software, y = Median, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(
    Metric ~ Contrast,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = software_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistical precision across all planned contrasts",
    subtitle = "Only protein groups with valid results in all four pipelines within each contrast",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
    strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 8),
    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_precision_all)
```

Across all 11 differential abundance contrasts, MaxDIA consistently exhibited the highest median standard errors and lowest median absolute t-statistics among the four DIA analysis pipelines. This pattern persisted when restricting each contrast to approximately 7,475 protein groups with valid estimates in all four pipelines. MaxDIA did not systematically produce smaller effect sizes; in seven contrasts, it exhibited the largest median absolute log2 fold change. Combined with its substantially higher protein-level residual variability, these findings indicate that increased statistical uncertainty is a major contributor to MaxDIA's lower differential abundance detection rate.

# - logfc_agreement_all
```{r da_logfc_agreement_all, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, dpi=300, out.width="100%", results="asis", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")
contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Collect finite log2 fold changes for all contrasts
logfc_all_long <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      Software = software,
      logFC = logFC
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Create one row per protein and contrast, with four pipeline columns
logfc_all_wide <- logfc_all_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(Contrast, Protein),
    names_from = Software,
    values_from = logFC
  )

# Six unique pipeline pairs
software_pairs <- combn(software_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Pairwise agreement metrics and scatterplots for each contrast
agreement_results <- list()
agreement_plots <- list()

for (contrast_name in contrast_order) {

  contrast_data <- logfc_all_wide |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  pair_data <- lapply(software_pairs, function(pair) {

    x <- contrast_data[[pair[1]]]
    y <- contrast_data[[pair[2]]]

    valid <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)

    data.frame(
      Protein = contrast_data$Protein[valid],
      Pipeline_1 = pair[1],
      Pipeline_2 = pair[2],
      Pair = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
      logFC_1 = x[valid],
      logFC_2 = y[valid]
    )
  }) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows()

  # Agreement statistics
  agreement_results[[contrast_name]] <- pair_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Pipeline_1, Pipeline_2, Pair) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Shared_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
      Pearson_r = cor(logFC_1, logFC_2, method = "pearson"),
      Spearman_rho = cor(logFC_1, logFC_2, method = "spearman"),
      Same_Direction_Percent = 100 * mean(
        sign(logFC_1) == sign(logFC_2)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Contrast = contrast_name, .before = 1)

  # Scatterplot: shared axes and identity line
  p <- ggplot(
    pair_data,
    aes(x = logFC_1, y = logFC_2)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.5,
      color = "#344054"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "#D55E00",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Pair, ncol = 3, scales = "fixed") +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Log2 fold-change agreement:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "Matched protein groups; dashed line indicates identical fold changes",
      x = "Pipeline 1 log2 fold change",
      y = "Pipeline 2 log2 fold change"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  agreement_plots[[contrast_name]] <- p

  cat("\n\n### ", contrast_name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(p)
}

# Combine agreement statistics across all 11 contrasts
logfc_agreement_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(agreement_results) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order),
    Pipeline_1,
    Pipeline_2
  )

cat("\n\n### Pairwise fold-change agreement summary\n\n")

print(logfc_agreement_summary, n = Inf)
```

Pairwise comparison of protein-level log2 fold changes across 11 differential abundance contrasts revealed substantial differences in agreement among DIA analysis pipelines. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN showed the strongest overall concordance, with a median Pearson correlation of 0.719 and median directional agreement of 77.5%. DIA-NN and Spectronaut also exhibited relatively strong agreement (median r = 0.671). In contrast, comparisons involving MaxDIA consistently showed lower correlations, ranging from median r = 0.378 to 0.500, and lower directional agreement, ranging from 63.9% to 68.0%. Agreement was contrast-dependent, with stronger concordance for prominent treatment-associated responses and weaker concordance for the JNK inhibitor effect at 6h. Combined with MaxDIA's higher residual variability and standard errors, these findings suggest that pipeline-specific differences in protein quantification and statistical precision contribute to variability in differential abundance results. Nevertheless, cross-pipeline agreement alone cannot establish which pipeline provides the most accurate estimates.

# - volcano_all
```{r da_volcano_all, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, dpi=300, out.width="100%", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")
contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Significance threshold
fdr_cutoff <- 0.05

# Output folders
volcano_dir <- "figures/volcano_plots"
individual_dir <- file.path(volcano_dir, "individual")
combined_dir <- file.path(volcano_dir, "combined")

dir.create(individual_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(combined_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Collect differential abundance results
volcano_data <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC),
      is.finite(adjPval),
      adjPval >= 0,
      adjPval <= 1
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Software = software,
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      logFC = logFC,
      adjPval = adjPval
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Contrast = factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order),
    Significant = adjPval < fdr_cutoff,
    neg_log10_FDR = -log10(pmax(adjPval, .Machine$double.xmin))
  )

# Count significant proteins per contrast and pipeline
volcano_summary <- volcano_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Tested_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
    Significant_Proteins = sum(Significant),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(volcano_summary, n = Inf)

# File-safe contrast names
safe_filename <- function(x) {
  gsub(
    "_+$", "",
    gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
  )
}

# Store generated plots
volcano_plots <- list()
volcano_combined <- list()

for (i in seq_along(contrast_order)) {

  contrast_name <- contrast_order[i]

  contrast_data <- volcano_data |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  # Common limits across pipelines within this contrast
  x_limit <- max(abs(contrast_data$logFC), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  y_limit <- max(contrast_data$neg_log10_FDR, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05

  x_limit <- max(x_limit, 0.5)
  y_limit <- max(y_limit, -log10(fdr_cutoff) * 1.1)

  # Individual volcano plots
  for (software in software_order) {

    plot_data <- contrast_data |>
      dplyr::filter(Software == software)

    n_sig <- sum(plot_data$Significant)

    p <- ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR)
    ) +
      geom_point(
        data = function(d) d[!d$Significant, ],
        color = "#B8BDC7",
        alpha = 0.45,
        size = 0.65
      ) +
      geom_point(
        data = function(d) d[d$Significant, ],
        color = unname(software_colors[software]),
        alpha = 0.7,
        size = 0.8
      ) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff),
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "#667085",
        linewidth = 0.5
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        color = "#98A2B3",
        linewidth = 0.4
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
        ylim = c(0, y_limit)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = software,
        subtitle = paste0(n_sig, " proteins at FDR < 0.05"),
        x = "Log2 fold change",
        y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )

    volcano_plots[[paste(contrast_name, software, sep = " | ")]] <- p

    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = file.path(
        individual_dir,
        sprintf(
          "%02d_%s_%s.png",
          i,
          safe_filename(contrast_name),
          safe_filename(software)
        )
      ),
      plot = p,
      width = 7,
      height = 5.5,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  # Four-panel comparison with common axes
  combined_plot <- ggplot(
    contrast_data,
    aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[!d$Significant, ],
      color = "#B8BDC7",
      alpha = 0.4,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[d$Significant, ],
      aes(color = Software),
      alpha = 0.65,
      size = 0.65
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "#667085"
    ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      color = "#98A2B3"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Software, ncol = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = software_colors) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
      ylim = c(0, y_limit)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Differential abundance:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "FDR < 0.05; identical axes across all four pipelines",
      x = "Log2 fold change",
      y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  volcano_combined[[contrast_name]] <- combined_plot

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      combined_dir,
      sprintf(
        "%02d_%s.png",
        i,
        safe_filename(contrast_name)
      )
    ),
    plot = combined_plot,
    width = 12,
    height = 9,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  print(combined_plot)
}

# Save summary table
utils::write.csv(
  volcano_summary,
  file = file.path(volcano_dir, "volcano_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat(
  "\nSaved 44 individual volcano plots,",
  "11 four-panel figures, and 1 summary CSV to:",
  normalizePath(volcano_dir),
  "\n"
)
```

# - agreement across all

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 7. Log2FC agreement across all 11 contrasts
# ============================================================

logfc_all_wide_68 <- quantitative_all_68 |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(logFC)) |>
  dplyr::select(Contrast, Protein, Software, logFC) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(Contrast, Protein),
    names_from = Software,
    values_from = logFC
  )

agreement_results_68 <- list()
agreement_plots_68 <- list()

agreement_dir_68 <- "figures/da_logfc_agreement_68"
dir.create(
  agreement_dir_68,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

safe_filename_68 <- function(x) {
  gsub("_+$", "", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x))
}

for (i in seq_along(contrast_order_68)) {

  contrast_name <- contrast_order_68[i]

  contrast_data <- logfc_all_wide_68 |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  pair_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(pipeline_pairs_68, function(pair) {

      x <- contrast_data[[pair[1]]]
      y <- contrast_data[[pair[2]]]
      valid <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)

      data.frame(
        Pipeline_1 = pair[1],
        Pipeline_2 = pair[2],
        Pair = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
        logFC_1 = x[valid],
        logFC_2 = y[valid]
      )
    })
  )

  agreement_results_68[[contrast_name]] <- pair_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Pipeline_1, Pipeline_2, Pair) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Shared_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
      Pearson_r = cor(logFC_1, logFC_2),
      Spearman_rho = cor(
        logFC_1, logFC_2, method = "spearman"
      ),
      Same_Direction_Percent = 100 * mean(
        sign(logFC_1) == sign(logFC_2)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Contrast = contrast_name, .before = 1)

  p <- ggplot(
    pair_data,
    aes(x = logFC_1, y = logFC_2)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5, color = "#344054"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1, intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed", color = "#D55E00"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Pair, ncol = 3) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Log2 fold-change agreement:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "Matched protein groups; dashed line: y = x",
      x = "Pipeline 1 log2 fold change",
      y = "Pipeline 2 log2 fold change"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  agreement_plots_68[[contrast_name]] <- p

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(
      agreement_dir_68,
      sprintf(
        "%02d_%s.png",
        i, safe_filename_68(contrast_name)
      )
    ),
    plot = p,
    width = 12,
    height = 8,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )
}

logfc_agreement_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  agreement_results_68
)

print(logfc_agreement_summary_68, n = Inf)

utils::write.csv(
  logfc_agreement_summary_68,
  file.path(agreement_dir_68, "logfc_agreement_summary_68.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
